factor/bowl: Take the simplest function to walk down, a bowl: f of x equals a x squared, where a, a positive number, sets how steep it is. Its minimum is at zero. Here a is one, and x starts at one.
factor/grad: Its gradient is two a x. So one step takes x to x, minus eta times two a x. That step size, eta, is called the learning rate.
factor/factor: Pull out the x, and every step just multiplies x by the same factor: one minus two a eta. With eta at zero point three, that is zero point four.
factor/shift: Now slide the bowl so its bottom sits at three: f of x equals a times x minus three, squared. Each slope is the old one at the same distance from the bottom, so the gradient is two a, times x minus three.
factor/dist: From x equals four, with eta at zero point three, the distance x minus three goes one, zero point four, zero point one six: the same factor, one minus two a eta, every step. Sliding the bowl moves the minimum, and nothing else.
race/small: With a learning rate of zero point zero five, the factor is zero point nine. Each step keeps ninety percent of x, and the ball creeps.
race/good: With zero point three, the factor is zero point four. x shrinks fast and slides straight in.
race/zig: With zero point eight, the factor is minus zero point six. Each step overshoots to the other side, but lands closer: it zigzags in.
race/big: With one point one, the factor is minus one point two. Every overshoot lands farther out, and the steps blow up.
limit/line: Plot the factor against eta. It starts at one and falls in a straight line as eta grows.
limit/half: At eta equals one over two a, it is zero: a single step lands right on the minimum.
limit/edge: At one over a, it reaches minus one, and x bounces between two points forever. Any larger, and it blows up.
limit/solve: Why one over a? Set the factor to minus one: one minus two a eta equals minus one. Then two a eta is two, and eta is one over a.
limit/steep: A steeper bowl, a bigger a, makes the line fall faster, so it reaches minus one sooner: at a half, when a is two. The largest learning rate that does not diverge, written eta max, is one over a.
try/p1: Try one: f of x is four x squared, x is three, and eta is zero point one. Where does one step land?
try/a1: The gradient is two times four times three: twenty-four. The step is zero point one times that, two point four. So x goes from three to zero point six.
try/check: Check with the factor: one minus two times four times zero point one is zero point two, and zero point two times three is zero point six.
try/p2: Now slide that bowl to three: f is four times x minus three, squared. What is the largest eta that does not diverge?
try/a2: Sliding moves only the minimum, so a is still four. Set the factor to minus one: one minus eight eta is minus one, so eight eta is two, and eta is zero point two five.
